title: Present Perfect Continuous: have been + -ing
grammarTitle: Present Perfect Continuous — Duration and Evidence
grammarNote:
Present Perfect Continuous (have/has been + -ing) описывает действие, которое началось в прошлом и:
1) ВСЁ ЕЩЁ ПРОДОЛЖАЕТСЯ сейчас, OR
2) ТОЛЬКО ЧТО ЗАВЕРШИЛОСЬ и оставило видимый результат

Ключевые слова: for (на протяжении), since (с тех пор как), how long (как долго), all day/week/morning, recently, lately.

grammarTable.subject: I / You / We / They
grammarTable.example: "I have been studying English for two years." / "They have been working since 9 a.m."

grammarTable.subject: He / She / It
grammarTable.example: "She has been preparing for the interview for months." / "He has been coding all night."

grammarTable.subject: Negative
grammarTable.example: "I haven't been sleeping well." / "She hasn't been eating much."

grammarTable.subject: Question
grammarTable.example: "How long have you been working here?" / "Has she been studying today?"

grammarTable.subject: FOR
grammarTable.example: "FOR three months" / "FOR an hour" / "FOR ages" — length of time.

grammarTable.subject: SINCE
grammarTable.example: "SINCE 2022" / "SINCE Monday" / "SINCE I was 15" — point when it started.

grammarExtra.title: Present Perfect Continuous vs Present Perfect Simple

rows.example: "I've been reading this book." (I'm still reading it / process matters)
"I've read this book." (I finished it — result is important)
"You look tired." "I've been working all night." (explains WHY I look tired)

rows.form: Simple: states the NUMBER of times done
rows.example: "I've read three books this month." (counting completions — NOT "been reading three books")

grammarExtra.title: When to use Present Perfect Continuous

rows.example: "I've been studying English FOR two years." (started 2 years ago, still studying now) ✅
"My hands are dirty — I've been fixing the car." (just stopped, dirty hands = evidence) ✅

rows.form: Explaining a current state or visible sign
rows.example: "Why are you sweating? I've been running." (the running explains the sweat) ✅
"She's been working really hard lately." (recently, up to this moment) ✅

grammarExtra.title: Stative verbs — NOT used in continuous

rows.example: ✗ "I've been knowing her for years." → ✅ "I've known her for years." (stative = use Simple!)
✗ "I've been loving this job." → ✅ "I've loved this job." / "I love this job." ✅
✗ "She's been owning this car for 5 years." → ✅ "She's owned this car for 5 years."
✗ "It's been seeming difficult." → ✅ "It seems difficult." / "It has seemed difficult." ✅
✅ "I've been studying SINCE 2020." (2020 = starting point → SINCE) or "FOR 4 years" (duration).

rows.form: ✗ "She has been working here since 3 years."
rows.example: ✅ "She has been working here FOR 3 years." (3 years = duration → FOR!)
✅ "I've KNOWN her for years." — stative verbs use Simple, not Continuous!

grammarTip:
Present Perfect Continuous = have/has + been + -ing

ФОРМУЛА:
Subject + have/has + been + verb-ing

Для ПРОДОЛЖИТЕЛЬНОСТИ:
FOR + период: "for three months" ✅
SINCE + точка: "since 2022" / "since Monday" ✅

Когда использовать Continuous vs Simple:
Continuous → ПРОЦЕСС важен / действие длится:
"I've been working here." (ещё работаю)

Simple → РЕЗУЛЬТАТ / завершение:
"I've finished the project." (готово)
"I've read 5 books." (считаю — не "been reading 5 books")

⚠️ Stative verbs → НЕ continuous:
✗ "I've been knowing her"
✅ "I've known her for years."

FOR vs SINCE:
FOR = продолжительность: for 2 years, for ages
SINCE = начало: since 2020, since Monday, since I was 15

exercises.text: She looks exhausted. She ___ all night.
exercises.hint: Visible evidence (she looks exhausted) explains ongoing/just-stopped action = Present Perfect Continuous. "She HAS BEEN WORKING all night." ✅
"three years" = duration/period → FOR. "FOR three years." ✅ (SINCE = starting point, like "since 2021")

exercises.text: "She's been working at DataBridge ___ she graduated."
exercises.hint: "she graduated" = a starting point in time → SINCE. "SINCE she graduated." ✅

exercises.text: "I ___ (read) this article — it's really interesting." (still reading now)
exercises.hint: Process ongoing = Present Perfect Continuous. "I HAVE BEEN READING." ✅ (If I had finished: "I HAVE READ" ✅)
Counting completions → Present Perfect SIMPLE. "He HAS READ three books this month." ✅ (NOT "has been reading three books" — can't count with Continuous!)

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct form for a stative verb.
exercises.hint: "know" = stative verb → Present Perfect SIMPLE. "I'VE KNOWN her since secondary school." ✅ Never "been knowing"!
Question: "How long HAVE YOU BEEN STUDYING for the exam?" ✅

exercises.text: "She has been working here since 3 years." is correct.
exercises.hint: ✅ "She has been working here FOR 3 years." — duration (3 years) requires FOR, not SINCE!

exercises.text: "Why is your shirt wet?" — Best answer:
exercises.hint: Visible evidence (wet shirt) + explains current state = Perfect Continuous. "I'VE BEEN RUNNING." ✅
Duration ongoing → Present Perfect Continuous. "She HAS BEEN PREPARING for months." ✅

exercises.text: "I ___ (finish) the report — here it is." (completed, result matters)
exercises.hint: Completed result ready to hand over = Present Perfect SIMPLE. "I'VE FINISHED the report." ✅

exercises.text: "She ___ well lately — something must be wrong."
exercises.hint: Ongoing recent pattern → Present Perfect Continuous negative. "She HASN'T BEEN SLEEPING well lately." ✅

questions.text: Present Perfect Continuous is formed with:
"She has been working here ___." Which word fits?
questions.hint: "six months" = duration → FOR. "FOR six months." ✅ (SINCE = starting point)
SINCE + starting point (specific time). "SINCE 2021." ✅ (FOR + duration: "for three years")
"has been + -ing" = Present Perfect Continuous for she/he/it. ✅

questions.text: When is Present Perfect Continuous most appropriate?
opts: Actions still ongoing or just-stopped — duration or evidence
questions.correct: Actions still ongoing or just-stopped — duration or evidence
questions.hint: Use when: duration is the focus, action continues, OR visible evidence explains the current state. ✅
"know" = stative verb → CANNOT use Continuous. "I'VE KNOWN her since school." ✅ Never "been knowing"!

questions.text: "I've been reading" vs "I've read." Key difference:
"He has read 5 books this month." Can we say "been reading 5 books"?
opts: No — can't count with Continuous; use Simple for numbers
questions.correct: No — can't count with Continuous; use Simple for numbers
questions.hint: Counting completions → Simple. "He HAS READ 5 books." ✅ NOT "been reading 5 books."

questions.text: "You look tired." What's the most natural reply?
questions.hint: Explaining a visible state (looking tired) = Perfect Continuous. "I'VE BEEN WORKING all night." ✅
"How long HAVE YOU BEEN WORKING at WKU?" ✅ Question form of Present Perfect Continuous.

questions.text: "I've been knowing her for years." — What is wrong?
questions.hint: "know" = stative → use Simple. "I'VE KNOWN her for years." ✅ Never "been knowing"!

questions.text: "She hasn't been eating much." — This suggests:
opts: She ate a lot in the past
A recent pattern of not eating enough — visible concern
She will not eat in the future
questions.correct: A recent pattern of not eating enough — visible concern
questions.hint: Present Perfect Continuous negative = recent ongoing pattern with implication. ✅
"has been studying" = Perfect Continuous. Duration from 7 a.m. until now. ✅
FOR + period of time (three months, ages, two years). SINCE + starting point (2020, Monday). ✅

questions.text: "I've been working here since I was 18." — "since" is followed by:
questions.hint: SINCE + starting point in time. "since I was 18" = the moment it began. ✅

questions.text: Which sentence uses Present Perfect Continuous CORRECTLY?
opts: "He has been preparing for the interview for weeks."
questions.correct: "He has been preparing for the interview for weeks."
questions.hint: "He HAS BEEN PREPARING for the interview for weeks." ✅ Correct: have been + -ing + duration.
